relatedSnapshot.title: Turn on phone billing safely with automatic settlement setup
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Make phone billing turn on in one safe, approved step, so a billing setting can never stop a sales team from texting again. On 6 Oct 2026 the AI Acquisition Sales Team couldn't send texts for about two hours. Name 1 had started putting wallet money on hold for each text, and nothing was set up to finalise those holds. This programme stops expired holds from blocking a whole account and lets a workspace take new holds only when it's enrolled in settlement. Then it makes enrolment automatic, before ENG-14796 turns billing on for every Phone Calling workspace.

## Problem

Three things decide whether a workspace is billed today, and they don't agree. Texts and calls take a hold when Phone Calling and Name 1 are both on, or when the workspace has a settlement setup whose charging start has passed. Number renewals, number purchases and SMS registration fees look only at the two flags. Name 2 a hold needs the settlement setup and also Name 1. An admin creates the settlement setup by hand, in Admin, Workspaces, the row menu, Twilio billing.

A text hold lasts 23 hours. A hold that nothing finalises stays unresolved. Once it's within a minute of running out, a safety check refuses every new text, renewal, number purchase and SMS registration fee on that billing account. Users see "phone funding could not be verified. Please try again shortly", which retrying can't fix.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Text or call sent] --> B[2: hold only if enrolled]
  B --> C[Settlement finalises hold]
  B -- not finalised --> D[1: reconcile expired hold]
  D --> E[Account keeps working]
  F[3: automatic enrolment] --> C
```

The numbers show where each child changes the path. ENG-14810 (1) reconciles expired holds instead of leaving them to block the account. ENG-14811 (2) stops new holds when nothing can finalise them, and ENG-14812 (3) enrols workspaces automatically.

Incident evidence from the read-only production replica (not code-verified): the switch went on at 12:41 pm UTC on 5 Oct 2026. 117 texts sent with holds and none was finalised. The first holds ran out at 12:20 pm UTC on 6 Oct, and every text failed until we closed 121 old holds by hand at 2:33 pm UTC. Texts sent with holds finalised from 2:39 pm UTC.

## User experience

A workspace with phone billing just keeps working. If billing needs attention, users see a message that says what's wrong and who can fix it, and an admin sees the held items in the Twilio billing panel. A workspace that isn't enrolled in settlement keeps texting and calling without holds.

## What's included

1. ENG-14810: expired holds are reconciled against Autumn and Twilio evidence and closed only when no money can still move. Anything unclear goes to a review state that admins can see, and the error message says what's actually wrong.
2. ENG-14811: new holds start only when the workspace is enrolled in settlement. Work already paid for or reserved still finishes.
3. ENG-14812: approved workspaces are enrolled in settlement automatically, in safe stages, and blocked ones show the reason.

## Out of scope

* One settlement setup per billing account instead of per workspace. It changes about 25 call sites and the table keys, and 7 of the 329 workspaces with Phone Calling share a billing account (production replica, 6 Oct 2026). ENG-14812 leaves those 7 unenrolled with a warning.
* Removing the Name 1 flag and its remaining checks, which ENG-14796 owns.
* Sendblue billing, which ENG-12622 owns.
* Customer notices and the go-live approval, which ENG-12727 owns.

## Execution order

1. ENG-14810 and ENG-14811: start now, in parallel.
2. ENG-14796: merges after ENG-14811.
3. ENG-14812: after ENG-14810 and ENG-14811, and its production enrolment waits for the ENG-12727 approval.

## Decisions needed

* **Does an admin turning on Phone Calling for a workspace count as the production approval that** ENG-12727 **asks for?** Recommended: yes, when an admin turns it on for that workspace, because James wants billing to be automatic and the admin's action is recorded with their name. Partner-level enablement doesn't count until decided separately. Decider: James Keeble. Blocks: ENG-14812's production enrolment only.

## Name 3 and rollback

ENG-14810 and ENG-14811 ship behind the existing billing switches. ENG-14812 runs in report-only mode on production first, and the report is posted on ENG-14796 before any enrolment. A charging start date can't be removed, so undoing enrolment is a forward procedure. Stop new billed activity for the workspace through ENG-14811's enrolment check. Settlement, wallet-change recovery and cost reconciliation keep running for everything already held or owed. Don't pause "Charge verified usage" as a rollback, because that also stops settling existing liabilities. Never delete settlement records or forgive amounts due as a rollback step.

## Done when

* An expired hold can no longer block a billing account unless its provider outcome is truly unresolved, and those cases show in the Twilio billing panel.
* No path starts a new hold for a workspace that isn't enrolled in settlement.
* Approved workspaces are enrolled automatically, and the report lists every skipped workspace with its reason.
* ENG-14796 is unblocked.

## Implementation context

* Safety check: `assertNoExpiredPhoneFunding` in unsettled-funding.ts
* Manual setup: `configureTwilioBilling` in operations.ts
* Manual repair on 6 Oct 2026: 121 text holds (117 accepted, 4 unknown, all created before the 2:23 pm UTC charging start) were set to `settled` with a note. Settlement only rates costs incurred after the charging start, so these won't be charged. ENG-14810 reconciles each of them into its new closed or needs-review state, so `settled` keeps meaning "collected".
* Full research and evidence: AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Fill in email and text variables on the server when sending
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Personalized emails and texts are filled in by the rep's browser today, and the server only refuses anything that still contains `{{`. This moves the filling-in to the server on every send and schedule, so what goes out never depends on the browser, and workflow steps can use personalized templates too.

## Problem

In ENG-13831 (Acquisity/Acquisity#6485) the composer renders the message, then sends the finished text. The server checks that no variable is left, but it cannot confirm the values are right for that person, and an outdated browser tab can still send content it filled in earlier. Workflow send steps have no browser at all, so they cannot use personalized templates yet.

## User experience

Nothing changes in the composer: reps still preview, pick a company when a person has several, and add fallbacks. When they press Send or Schedule, the server fills in the variables for that person and sends exactly that. A scheduled message still keeps the exact text the rep reviewed. A missing value without a fallback still blocks the send with the same message it shows today.

## What's included

* Email send, reply, draft send and scheduled email; text send, scheduled text and Conversations reply take the saved template text, its format and the chosen company, and the server fills it in.
* Scheduled messages store the filled-in text at the moment they are scheduled, and still send that exact text later.
* If the person's details changed between preview and send, the send is refused and the rep is asked to preview again (so the message always matches what they saw).
* Email and text workflow steps can use a team personalized template and fill it in when the step runs, with the same retry safety as manual sends.
* The browser no longer keeps its own copy of the filled-in text for retries.

## Done when

* A personalized send from an outdated browser tab either sends correctly filled text or is refused; it never sends unfilled or stale variables.
* Scheduled personalized messages send the exact text reviewed at scheduling, even if the person or template changes later.
* A workflow email or text step using a team personalized template sends filled-in text, retries without sending twice, and stops with a clear error when a value is missing.
* Existing literal templates still send exactly as written.

## Open questions

* Preview versus send mismatch: refuse and ask for a fresh preview (recommended), or send the newest values. Recommended default: refuse, as the original ticket asks that reviewed content is what goes out.

## Implementation context

AI context.md holds the current send paths, the minimal server check this replaces, and the workflow retry contract.

## Overview

In v2 Conversations, a rep looking at someone who has only calls or emails can send them a first text from the thread composer, instead of seeing the composer disabled.

## Problem

The record page's "send text" path checks workspace membership and the sender's phone line, but not whether the rep may access that contact, unlike the reply path Conversations uses. It needs the same contact-access check before Conversations can use it.

## What's included

* The new-text send path applies the same contact-access check as the reply path, and still enforces opt-out.
* The v2 thread composer enables Text for people with a phone number and no text thread.
* If this is small it can ship inside ENG-14167 (one composer).

## Done when

* A rep can text a call-only or email-only person from the thread, and the new text thread appears.
* A rep who cannot access the contact is refused by the server.
* Opted-out numbers still cannot be texted.

## Design

Kit element: the SMS composer on a person with no text conversation. Design (full kit): Acquisity v2 Kit, Conversations, route `#/screen/crm-conversations` (private until James shares it).

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2: text and call a deal's person from the deal record
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep on a deal in the new CRM (record drawer or full deal page) can text the deal's person from the deal itself, the same way they can already call them. Today Text is missing on deals, and "Text back" on a call row jumps away to the person's page.

## Problem

Deals are where reps work, but texting means leaving the deal, finding the person and opening their Calls & Texts tab. With several people on one deal, it is easy to text the wrong one.

## User experience

* **Text in the action row**, next to Call, whenever calling is on for the workspace.
  * One linked person with a phone number: Text opens the deal's composer on Text, addressed to that person.
  * Several: Text asks which person (name and number), then opens the composer for the one picked.
  * None: Text is disabled and says why (no linked person, or no one has a phone number), in the same words as the deal's Call button. An opted-out person gets the person page's opt-out message.
* **The composer always shows who the text goes to** (name and number), so a deal with several people is never ambiguous.
* **Consent and do-not-contact rules are exactly the person page's.** An opted-out person shows the same "Texts are paused" block and cannot be sent to; a workspace with no phone number cannot text.
* **Text back from a call row** opens the deal's composer for the person that call was with. A call with no number, a number that matches no linked person, a number two linked people share, or a number that is not that person's texting number is never guessed: the rep sees a short message instead.
* **Call** keeps today's behaviour: one reachable person is called straight away, several are asked which.

## What's included

* The deal drawer and the full deal page, both behind the CRM v2 flag and the phone calling feature.
* Reuses today's text composer (templates, send later, placeholders, consent checks).
* Not included: texting several people at once, and texting a number other than a person's main number.

## Done when

* Text shows on a deal next to Call and follows the one, several and none rules above.
* The composer names the person and number the text will go to.
* An opted-out person cannot be texted from a deal, with the same message as the person page.
* Text back on a deal's call row opens the deal composer for that call's person, or explains why it cannot.
* Sending a text from a deal is tracked in product analytics (wired and unit-tested; not yet seen landing in PostHog).
* Checked in the browser in light and dark, in the drawer and on the full page, without sending a real text.

## Implementation context

* Follow-up to Acquisity/Acquisity#6564 (ENG-14192). Splits out the "A deal's drawer texts the main contact directly" item from ENG-14191.
* ENG-14230 touches the same record composer; merge carefully.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop showing "Texting is unavailable" while the text box is still checking
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep opens the text box on a person or deal, they sometimes see a red "Texting is unavailable. SMS is unavailable while consent status cannot be verified. Try again shortly." notice that disappears by itself. Nothing is actually wrong: the app is still checking whether the person accepts texts. This ticket shows that wait as a wait, and keeps the red notice for real problems, with a way to retry.

## Problem

Reported on the 30 Sep migration call: the notice showed for up to a minute on load, then went away. It looked like texting was broken during the busiest week of the move from Close.

Checked on main on 1 Oct: the text box treats "still checking" and "the check failed" as the same thing and shows the outage wording for both. The check retries quietly three times, so when the database is slow (the Close import was running) the wait, and the red notice, can last close to a minute. So this is not only a side effect of the import. Any slow moment shows a false outage.

The same wording also appears when retrying can never help, for example when the person was deleted or the rep is not allowed to see them.

## User experience

* **Checking:** the text box is disabled and says "Checking whether you can text this person…". No red notice. Sending stays blocked until the check finishes.
* **Check failed:** a notice says "We couldn't check whether this person accepts texts." with a Retry button. It no longer says "try again shortly" with nothing to press.
* **Not allowed or not found:** the notice says the rep cannot text this person, with no Retry.
* **Opted out or do not contact:** unchanged, these already have their own clear messages.

This applies to the text box on person and deal records (page and drawer), the in-call text box, and the first-text box in Conversations. The reply box in Conversations already behaves correctly.

## What's included

* The loading, failed and not-allowed states above on every surface that shows the notice today.
* Sending stays blocked while the answer is unknown. A text must never go out before the consent check has passed.
* Fewer silent retries, so a real failure shows within seconds instead of after a minute.
* Not included: making the consent check itself faster. It runs several database reads each time the box opens. If the notice still appears often after this change, that is a separate performance ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] With the consent check held open, the text box shows the checking state and no red notice, and Send is disabled.
- [ ] With the check failing, the notice offers Retry, and Retry re-runs the check and recovers when it succeeds.
- [ ] A person the rep cannot access, or a deleted person, shows a "cannot text this person" message without Retry and without "try again shortly".
- [ ] Opted-out and do-not-contact messages are unchanged.
- [ ] No text can be sent while the check is loading or failed.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a person page, a person drawer, a deal and the Conversations first-text box with the request blocked and then restored.

## Implementation context

* The cause is in `apps/web/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.ts` (about lines 62 to 73): `consentUnavailableReason` returns the outage message for `isError || isPending`. The sibling `actionDisabledReason` in the same hook already separates the two ("Checking SMS consent").
* Rendered by `TextBlockedNotice` in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.tsx` and by the first-text body in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/conversations/composer-text.tsx`. The Conversations reply notice in the same file already has a Retry pattern to copy.
* The query has no retry override, so the default three retries with back-off apply. The text box is mounted hidden from page load, so the check is often mid-retry when the rep opens Text.
* Several callers read `consentUnavailableReason` (`use-contact-sms-composer.ts`, the legacy Calls and Texts tab). Review them together when its meaning changes.
* Tests that pin today's behaviour and need updating: `tests/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.test.tsx` and `tests/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.test.tsx`.
* Not verified: the exact duration on 30 Sep. The one minute figure fits three slow attempts plus back-off but was not reproduced.

relatedSnapshot.title: Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

CRM gains a safe place to keep a text someone wants sent later, and the rules that turn that saved text into a real send exactly once.

## Problem

CRM has no way to remember a text that has not been sent yet. Everything in the texting flow assumes the send happens now. Before anything can be scheduled, there has to be a saved text that survives a server restart, a release, or two jobs waking up at the same moment, and one agreed set of rules for what may take that text and send it.

## Proposed fix

Add a place for CRM to keep scheduled texts, and the rules that go with it. CRM can save a text, take it for sending in a way that no second job can repeat, send it using the same texting route everything else uses, and record honestly what happened. Nothing schedules or sends anything yet.

## What's included

* One new place to keep scheduled texts, shared by the later email and management work.
* Saving a text without contacting the phone provider.
* Only one job can ever take a given text, so it cannot go out twice.
* That hold expires, so a job that fails partway does not leave the text stuck forever.
* Re-checking access, permission and phone-number ownership before sending.
* A marker unique to each saved text, so trying again can never turn into a second text going out.
* Honest results, keeping a clear failure and an unclear answer from the phone provider separate.

Not included: anything that watches the clock, any way for a person to schedule a text, any screen, and any analytics. Those are the two slices that follow. Cancelling, editing, changing the time, email, quiet hours, picture messages and bulk work are all outside this ticket entirely.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately. The texting, consent and duplicate-protection work this builds on is already finished.

## How it should work

* Saving a text never contacts the phone provider.
* Only one job can take a text. A second job finds nothing to do and stops.
* A hold that has expired can be taken again safely, because the unique marker means the phone provider is never contacted twice for the same text.
* If the person lost access, lost the phone number, or the recipient asked to stop, the text does not go out and the reason is recorded.
* A clear failure from the phone provider and an unclear answer are recorded differently, and an unclear answer never causes CRM to just send again and hope.

## Who can do what

Nothing is visible to anyone in this slice. Every read and write belongs to one workspace, and a text saved by another workspace can never be read, taken or sent.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: this slice adds no screen and changes nothing a person can see. The first visible change arrives with Let a rep schedule a text from the contact record.

## Done when

- [ ] Saving a text stores exactly one waiting text and never contacts the phone provider.
- [ ] When two jobs go for the same text at once, one sends it and the other does nothing.
- [ ] A hold that has expired can be taken again; one that is still live cannot.
- [ ] Losing access, losing the phone number, or a recipient who asked to stop each prevent the send, with the reason recorded.
- [ ] A clear failure and an unclear answer from the phone provider end up in visibly different states.
- [ ] A text that already went out can never be taken again.
- [ ] Tests cover each of the above.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled. How far ahead a text may be scheduled, and how much notice is needed, are decisions about what reps are allowed to do, and they are made in Let a rep schedule a text from the contact record.

## Expected outcome

The saved text and the sending rules that the next two slices, and both later scheduling tickets, all build on top of.

## Implementation context

First of three slices delivering Send one text later, and the only one that changes the database. Detailed planning, including the full itemised in-scope and out-of-scope lists, is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reply to texts and manage unread
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Audit update (2026-09-01; verified against origin/main **`b56300e23152`**):** The native Name 4 status and blocker relations now reflect the verified current scope. Existing description history is preserved below.

## Overview

A rep can continue an SMS conversation and manage their own read state without leaving Conversations.

## Problem

Current read state can be shared across the workspace, and SMS reply behavior is not integrated into the new Conversations screen. Email reliability work should not block the SMS MVP.

## Proposed fix

Add per-user CRM read state and connect the composer to the existing authorized SMS send-and-record path.

## What's included

* Per-user read and unread.
* CRM-local unread counts.
* Needs reply for SMS when the latest customer message has no later outbound response.
* Reply from an authorized phone number for the conversation.
* Sending, sent and failed states.
* Durable recording through the existing SMS path.
* Idempotent retry.

Not included: email display, email replies, bulk actions, generated replies, forwarding, reassignment or cadence management.

## Blocked by

* Build the all-activity Conversations screen.

## How it should work

* Read state is keyed to workspace, user and conversation.
* Opening may mark read for that user only.
* Mark unread persists through refresh.
* Needs reply is independent from unread.
* The server validates the real sending phone number.
* Successful sends appear once.
* Failed sends keep the draft and show retry.
* Retrying the same operation cannot send twice.

## Who can do what

A user may reply only when they can view the conversation and use its sender. Every read and write is workspace scoped.

## What the user sees

Read controls, counts, the SMS composer, disconnected-sender state, and sending, success or failure feedback. Email controls are absent.

## Done when

- [ ] Two users can hold different read states.
- [ ] Refresh does not overwrite CRM-local state.
- [ ] Needs reply matches the agreed SMS rule.
- [ ] SMS uses the correct sender.
- [ ] Success appears once.
- [ ] Retry cannot duplicate a text.
- [ ] Browser QA covers read, unread, needs reply, success, failure and disconnected sender.
- [ ] Permission and cross-workspace tests cover every mutation.

## Open questions

None: V1 is SMS only and keeps read state local.

## Expected outcome

Reps can work SMS conversations without false success, duplicate sends or shared unread state.

## Notification integration

**Notification and reply-state integration**

Personal notification read/dismiss state is separate from CRM per-user unread and shared Needs reply. Advance the user's read watermark only through content actually rendered in a focused, visible conversation. A send or Done action records the inbound revision it covers. If inbound A is followed by a pending reply and then inbound B, a delayed success or stale Done for A must leave B actionable. Queued/unknown send state is not proof of delivery; a later terminal failure creates action-required work without erasing newer inbound activity.

### Close guidance

Close SMS and MMS and Close Inbox guide direct text replies and read versus handled behavior. The covered-inbound revision requirement prevents newer replies being hidden.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Record every text message the platform sends
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12250. For THIS ticket: we have a messages table (`crm_message`) that stores text messages. **Every row in it today came from a message somebody sent to us.** Nothing we send is ever saved there. Sent texts only produce a line on the activity timeline, and texts sent by an automation produce nothing at all, not even a row in the database. Why it matters: our sales team sends 3,500 to 5,000 texts a day and we keep no history of any of them. Name 5 also wants texts counted as a sign that a rep is actively working a lead, which decides whether that lead can be handed to an SDR. That rule cannot exist while sent texts are missing.

**Size:** L · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** nothing · **MVP****
****How it should work (Close reference):** <url>

### Overview

After this ticket, every text the platform sends is saved with the message provider's own id and the name of the rep who sent it, exactly like received texts already are. Automated texts are saved too, marked as automated.

### Problem

Five separate holes:

1. **Sent texts are never written to** `crm_message`**.** `apps/web/trpc/routers/sms.ts:104-123` writes only a timeline event.
2. `crm_message` **has no rep column at all.** No user id, no sender, nothing. Confirmed against the migration history. So even received texts cannot be attributed beyond "the rep who owns that phone line".
3. **The provider's message id is thrown away.** `sms.ts:138` returns it to the browser and discards it. The knock-on effect: Sendblue sends us a delivery confirmation webhook that looks the message up by that id (`apps/web/app/api/webhooks/sendblue/outbound/route.ts`), and because no sent message ever carries one, **that webhook matches zero rows every single time it fires.**
4. **Three automated send paths write nothing whatsoever**: `apps/web/plugins/workflows/sms/steps/send-message.ts:100`, `apps/web/plugins/workflows/sendblue/steps/send-message.ts:151`, `apps/web/plugins/workflows/phone-numbers/steps/send-sms.ts:94`.
5. **One send path skips the provider router entirely.** The `sendSms` procedure in `apps/web/trpc/routers/phone-numbers.ts` (line 1770) calls the Twilio service directly on line 1788, so a text from a Sendblue line sent through that procedure goes out of the wrong account. **→ Split out to** ENG-12301**. Not delivered by this ticket.** (The `:1979` cited here originally is `validatePhoneNumber`, ~200 lines away — corrected 2026-08-05.)

Also, the timeline event does not record which provider sent the message, so Twilio text messages and Sendblue iMessages cannot be told apart afterwards.

### Solution

* Add a sender column to `crm_message` for the rep, plus a flag or source field marking automated sends. **Agree the exact shape with A6 (**ENG-12252) so there is one convention, not two. Whichever ticket starts first writes it down.
* Write a `crm_message` row on every send, from **one shared place**, storing the provider's message id, the provider name, and the message type (text message versus iMessage).
* Route the three automation steps through that same shared place, so there is exactly one way a text leaves the platform. **The direct-Twilio procedure (**`phoneNumbers.sendSms`**) is split out to** ENG-12301 — its provider-routing half has since been absorbed by PR #5895, leaving only the recording half there.
* Remove the rule that skips recording when the text has no contact attached (`sms.ts:104`). Record it against the phone number instead.
* Confirm the Sendblue delivery webhook now finds and updates the right message.

### Scope

* In: the sender and automation columns, one shared send-and-record path, **four of the** **five** send routes moved onto it (the fifth, `phoneNumbers.sendSms`, is ENG-12301), provider and message type recorded, delivery webhook verified working.
* Out of scope: counting texts on a manager screen (B6), opt-out handling (C3), scheduling (C4), WhatsApp (not supported at all).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A text sent from a contact record creates a message row with the provider's id, the sending rep, the provider name, and whether it went as a text message or an iMessage.
2. A text sent by an automation creates a message row marked as automated, with no rep credited.
3. A text sent to a number with no contact record still creates a message row.
4. The Sendblue delivery confirmation webhook updates the matching message. Verified against a real send, not a unit test alone. **⚠ Verified in code only as of PR #5900** — a real send needs live Sendblue credentials, a handset and a publicly reachable webhook, so the PR asks for this to be read as "verified-in-code but not verified-in-production". Do not close this ticket as fully met until that production check has actually been run.
5. Sending from a Sendblue line goes out through Sendblue regardless of which screen or procedure was used. **→ Split out to** ENG-12301 **(blocked by** ENG-12263**). Not delivered by this ticket.** Criterion kept here for history; see the comments for why.
6. Counting "texts sent by this rep today, excluding automated ones" is a single query.

### Design (Name 6)

Backend ticket — for reference, where recorded texts render: 12 · contact record — calls & texts (mixed SMS + call log with delivery state) and 38 · conversations — call thread. Full screen map on master ENG-12250.

relatedSnapshot.title: Show that a scheduled text is held for contact hours and when it will send
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a scheduled text is waiting for contact hours to open, the scheduled messages list says so and shows when it will go out, instead of showing a plain Pending past its scheduled time.

## Problem

Once texts can be held, a rep will see a message whose scheduled time has passed still marked Pending, with no explanation. That looks like a failure and invites a cancel and reschedule that is not needed.

## Proposed fix

The scheduled messages list recognises a held text and shows a Name 7 state with the time it will send and the reason, in the viewer's timezone with the zone shown, matching how scheduled times are already displayed. Cancel stays available on a held text.

## What's included

* The held state in the shared scheduled-message list components and the row.
* The list data carrying the release time and hold reason.
* Tests for the held row and for the transition back to Pending and then Sent.

Not included: any change to the hold itself, and any editing or rescheduling of a held text.

## Blocked by

* Hold a scheduled text that comes due outside contact hours until they open

## How it should work

* A pending text whose release time is in the future because of contact hours shows as Name 7, with "Sends at" and the time in the viewer's timezone.
* A pending text that has not yet reached its scheduled time shows as Pending, as today.
* A held text that is picked up and sent moves through Sending to Sent like any other.
* Cancelling a held text works exactly as cancelling a pending one.

## Who can do what

Same visibility as the scheduled messages list today: the creator sees their own, managers see what their team scope covers.

## What the user sees

A Name 7 badge on the row with the release time and a one-line reason such as "Outside contact hours for this contact". Hovering or expanding shows the contact's local time if known. Cancel remains on the row.

## Done when

- [ ] A held text shows as Name 7 with its release time in the viewer's timezone and the zone shown.
- [ ] A text not yet due still shows as Pending.
- [ ] A held text can be cancelled from the list.
- [ ] After the window opens and the text sends, the row shows Sent.
- [ ] Tests cover the held row and the state changes.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Reps can tell a held text from a stuck one at a glance and trust that it will go out.

## Implementation context

Fifth of five slices under Quiet hours: never call or text outside agreed times. Extends the components from Show scheduled-message states in reusable CRM components. Detailed planning is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let a rep schedule a text from the contact record
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep writes a text on a contact record, picks a future date and time, and CRM confirms it will go out then.

## Problem

CRM can now hold a scheduled text and send it, but there is no way for a person to create one. The composer on the contact record only sends immediately, so a rep who wants to reach someone at a better moment has to remember to come back and do it by hand.

## Proposed fix

Add Send later beside the existing Send in the Calls and Texts composer, with date and time controls that show the rep's own timezone. Choosing a time saves the message and confirms it, without contacting the phone provider. Send now keeps working exactly as it does today.

## What's included

* Send later beside the current Send action.
* Date and time controls showing the rep's active timezone.
* A clear message when the chosen time is not in the future, too soon, or too far ahead.
* Confirmation naming who the text goes to and when.
* A visibly different message when the text could not be saved at all.
* Checks that the rep can text and owns the chosen number, both when scheduling and again when the text sends.

Not included: any list of what is scheduled, any badge in the conversation, and any way to cancel. Those belong to Show and cancel scheduled messages. Editing, rescheduling, bulk work, quiet hours, MMS, attachments, templates and email are all outside this ticket.

## Blocked by

* Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice

This ticket does not depend on Send scheduled texts at the right time and can be built at the same time as it. Scheduling only has to save the text. CRM finds it and sends it separately, so the two can be worked on and merged in either order.

## How it should work

* Send now behaves exactly as it does today.
* Send later needs a time in the future and shows which timezone that time is in.
* Scheduling saves the message and never contacts the phone provider.
* A rep can only schedule when they can text right now and the chosen number is theirs.
* Another workspace can never schedule against, or read, this message.
* Saving the text is the whole job. Nothing else has to happen at the moment of scheduling, because CRM finds the text and sends it separately.
* If saving fails, the rep is told clearly that nothing was saved, so they can try again rather than assume it is handled.

## Who can do what

A rep can schedule from a contact they can already text, using a number already assigned to them. The same checks run again when the text actually sends, so access removed in between prevents delivery.

## What the user sees

* Send later beside the existing Send in the contact's Calls and Texts composer.
* Date and time controls, with the rep's active timezone shown so there is no ambiguity about which clock the time refers to.
* An inline message when the chosen time is not in the future, is sooner than the minimum notice, or is further ahead than allowed.
* A confirmation naming the recipient and the scheduled time, rather than the usual sent confirmation.
* A distinct failure message when the text could not be saved, worded so it is clearly different from a text that failed to send.
* The Send later control unavailable, with the existing reason shown, when the contact has asked to stop receiving texts.
* Nothing at all in sample data mode, consistent with the rest of the composer.
* At its scheduled time, the text appearing once in the conversation like any other.

## Done when

- [ ] Send now still works exactly as before.
- [ ] Send later saves one record that belongs only to this workspace, and never contacts the phone provider.
- [ ] A time that is not in the future, is too soon, or is too far ahead is refused with a clear and distinguishable message.
- [ ] Confirmation names the recipient and the scheduled time in the rep's timezone.
- [ ] A failure to save the text looks different from a text that failed to send.
- [ ] Another workspace cannot schedule against this contact, and a rep without texting access cannot schedule at all.
- [ ] A rep cannot schedule from a number that is not theirs.
- [ ] The composer works at normal and narrow widths.
- [ ] Browser QA proves both Send now and Send later, including a scheduled text arriving.
- [ ] Activation events are verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

* How far ahead a text may be scheduled. Recommended default: 12 months.
* How much notice is required before the scheduled time. Recommended default: one minute.
* Whether to ship before reps can see or cancel what they scheduled. Until Show and cancel scheduled messages ships, a rep who schedules a text has no way to view it or take it back. Recommended default: ship anyway and treat that invisibility as expected during QA rather than a defect, on the basis that the management ticket follows closely. Worth revisiting if that ticket is likely to wait weeks.
* Whether Send later is a split button or a separate secondary action. Recommended default: whichever matches the composer's existing visual weight, worth one design glance before building.

## Expected outcome

A rep can prepare a text while the conversation is fresh and trust CRM to deliver it later, without keeping a reminder somewhere else.

## Implementation context

One of three slices delivering Send one text later. Contains no database change. Detailed planning, including the full itemised in-scope and out-of-scope lists, is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Send one text later
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep can write one text from CRM, choose a future date and time, and trust CRM to send it once from the selected phone number.

## Problem

The current CRM text flow sends immediately. There is no durable record for a manually scheduled text, no delayed execution flow, and no status explaining whether a future send is waiting, sent or failed.

## Proposed fix

Add the shared scheduled-message foundation and use it for the first complete channel slice. Save the text and send time, then let a background worker use the existing recorded, consent-aware and duplicate-safe SMS path.

## What's included

* A scheduled-message record shared by the later email and management tickets.
* A background event and worker.
* Send later in the real contact Calls & Texts composer.
* One recipient and one plain-text SMS.
* Message body, contact, creator, selected sender and send time saved at creation.
* Pending, sending, sent, failed and unknown execution states.
* Send-time membership, permission, sender and consent checks.
* A stable operation key based on the scheduled-message ID.
* The resulting text in normal CRM message and activity history.

Not included: email scheduling, editing, rescheduling, bulk work, quiet hours, MMS, workflow SMS refactoring or the management page.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice: somewhere safe to keep a scheduled text, and the rules that turn it into exactly one send.

### Wave 2: starts when priority 1 completes

Parallel: Send scheduled texts at the right time and Let a rep schedule a text from the contact record. Neither depends on the other, so they can be built by different people and merged in either order. With capacity for only one, start the lower-numbered one first.

2. Send scheduled texts at the right time: due texts are found and sent once, through the same texting route everything else uses. Blocked by Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice.
3. Let a rep schedule a text from the contact record: Send later in the contact composer. Blocked by Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice.

Cross-wave overlap: None. Nothing can start before priority 1 is finished, because both remaining tickets read the saved text and the sending rules it creates. Once priority 1 has landed, the other two touch different files and cannot conflict with each other.

## Blocked by

None. The required SMS recording, sender-routing, consent and idempotency foundations are already complete.

## How it should work

* Send now keeps the existing behaviour.
* Send later requires a future time and shows the active timezone.
* Save the record before publishing its background event.
* Atomically claim a pending message before sending.
* Reuse the existing shared SMS path.
* If membership, permission, sender assignment or consent changes, do not send.
* Retries reuse the same operation key.
* A hard provider failure becomes failed. An ambiguous response becomes unknown and is not blindly resent.
* Save the CRM message and provider result once known.

## Who can do what

A rep can schedule only when they currently have SMS access and the selected number is assigned to them. The same checks run again at execution. Other workspaces cannot read, execute or change the message.

## What the user sees

* Send later beside the current Send action.
* Date and time controls with timezone.
* Validation for a time that is not in the future.
* Confirmation with recipient and scheduled time.
* A clear queueing failure.
* The text appearing once in history after execution.

## Done when

- [ ] Scheduling creates one workspace-scoped pending record without calling the provider.
- [ ] The worker sends at or after the selected time through the shared SMS path.
- [ ] Consent and sender authorization are rechecked at execution.
- [ ] Duplicate execution contacts the provider no more than once.
- [ ] Hard failure and unknown provider outcome remain distinct.
- [ ] The successful text appears once with correct rep attribution.
- [ ] Tests cover invalid time, cross-workspace access, revoked permission, reassigned sender, STOP after scheduling, duplicate workers and provider uncertainty.
- [ ] Browser QA proves Send now and Send later.
- [ ] Activation events are verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

* Maximum horizon. Recommended default: 12 months.
* Minimum lead time. Recommended default: one minute.

## Expected outcome

Reps can safely queue a normal one-to-one text without creating a second SMS implementation or risking duplicate delivery.

## Implementation context

Detailed point-in-time implementation planning is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Send scheduled texts at the right time
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

CRM notices when a scheduled text has come due and actually sends it, once, through the normal texting path, so it lands in the conversation like any other text.

## Problem

The saved record and the sending rules exist, but nothing ever notices that a message has come due. Something has to watch the clock, and it has to survive a background job going missing, a release landing in the middle of a wait, and two jobs waking up on the same message.

## Proposed fix

A recurring check finds messages that are due and hands each one to a background job. The job picks the message up using the rules already agreed, and sends it through the same texting route everything else uses. Because the send time is read from saved data rather than held in a sleeping background job, a job that goes missing is simply picked up on the next pass instead of being lost.

## What's included

* A recurring check that finds due messages and hands them out one at a time.
* A background job that picks up and sends a single message.
* One slow or failing text cannot hold up the others in the same run.
* Recording the result: sent, failed, or an unclear answer from the phone provider.
* The sent text appearing once in normal CRM message and activity history, credited to the right rep.

Not included: any way for a person to create a scheduled message, which arrives in the next slice. Testing and QA insert records by hand. No interface and no analytics. Chasing an unclear answer from the phone provider down to a final one is also out; this slice only has to record it honestly and stop. Cancelling, email, quiet hours and sequences are outside this ticket entirely.

## Blocked by

* Save a scheduled text so it cannot be lost or sent twice

## How it should work

* Only messages that are actually due and still waiting are picked up.
* A message is picked up before anything is sent.
* Two jobs on the same message result in at most one text.
* A background job that goes missing is recovered on the next pass rather than lost.
* If access, phone-number ownership or the recipient's wishes changed since the message was saved, it does not send and says why.
* A clear failure from the phone provider and an unclear answer stay distinguishable, and an unclear answer never causes CRM to just send again and hope.

## Who can do what

No new permissions and no new controls. Every query is scoped to one workspace, and no job can act on another workspace's message.

## What the user sees

Nothing new to click. The one visible change is the outcome: a text that was scheduled arrives at its time and appears once in the contact's conversation and activity history, credited to the rep who wrote it, exactly like a text sent by hand. A text that could not be sent stays out of the conversation rather than appearing as delivered.

## Done when

- [ ] A due message sends at or after its scheduled time through the same texting route everything else uses.
- [ ] The text appears once in CRM history with the correct rep credited.
- [ ] Duplicate background jobs for one message contact the phone provider at most once.
- [ ] A message whose background job never arrives still sends on a later pass.
- [ ] Someone who asked to stop after the message was saved does not receive it.
- [ ] Losing access or having the phone number reassigned prevents the send.
- [ ] A clear failure and an unclear answer from the phone provider end in different states.
- [ ] The recurring check ignores messages that are not yet due and messages already handled.
- [ ] Tests cover each of the above.

## Open questions

* How often the check runs. Recommended default: every minute, which matches the minimum notice a rep must give.
* How many messages one pass handles. Recommended default: start conservative and record when the limit is reached, so a backlog is visible rather than silent.

## Expected outcome

Scheduled texts actually go out, on time, once, with no way for a lost background job to silently swallow one.

## Implementation context

Second of three slices delivering Send one text later. Contains no database change. Detailed planning, including the full itemised in-scope and out-of-scope lists and the reasoning behind the timing approach, is in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop expired phone holds from blocking a whole billing account
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This child of ENG-14809 makes sure an expired hold can't silently take a team offline again, without losing track of money. Today a hold that nothing finalises blocks every new text, renewal, number purchase and SMS registration fee on its billing account until someone fixes the database by hand.

## Problem

Holds that Twilio accepted, or whose send outcome is unknown, leave that state only when settlement finalises them, and settlement skips holds whose lock has already run out. But an expired lock doesn't prove that no money will move. Twilio's real cost can still arrive, and settlement can then debit the wallet directly. An earlier wallet change at Autumn may also have an unknown outcome. So we can't close a hold just because it's old. There's also no state that means "closed without collecting", so the manual repair on 6 Oct 2026 had to use `settled`, which normally means the money was collected. Call holds have no expiry at all: they leave the spendable balance only when verified, rated costs transfer them.

## How it works

Today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Hold lock runs out] --> B[Stays accepted or unknown]
  B --> C[Safety check blocks account]
```

After this change:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Hold lock runs out] --> B[NEW: reconcile with evidence]
  B -- no money can move --> C[NEW: closed, not collected]
  B -- unclear --> D[NEW: needs review state]
  D --> E[Shown in Twilio billing panel]
```

Only holds that evidence proves are finished leave the safety check. Unclear ones still block, but now they're visible and recoverable instead of hidden.

## What's included

* Two new hold states, added by migration: "closed, not collected" and "needs review". Both keep the amount, the Autumn wallet change ID, the Twilio account and message IDs, the reason and the charge status.
* A scheduled reconciliation job that checks each expired accepted or unknown text hold against Autumn wallet changes and Twilio cost evidence. It closes a hold only when no wallet change can still apply and any late cost is handled by the existing settlement group and its idempotency record. Otherwise it moves the hold to needs review and recovers the wallet change.
* The safety check keeps blocking for unresolved or unknown provider outcomes, and stops blocking for holds the job has closed. The change runs under the billing-account lock, and tests cover the one-minute boundary.
* Call holds: recover missing call status and cost evidence, then transfer exposure through the existing reconciliation path. Age alone never clears a call hold, and ambiguous calls stay reserved for review.
* The Twilio billing panel lists holds that need review, with their reason.
* Error copy: when billing blocks a send, the message names the cause and who can fix it, for example "Phone billing needs attention. Ask a workspace admin to check phone billing." Keep "try again shortly" only for real temporary failures.
* Reconcile each of the 121 holds from the 6 Oct 2026 manual repair against provider evidence. Move a hold to closed only when it meets the closed-state rules, and keep unclear ones in needs review.

## How it should work

* The job is safe to rerun and never closes a hold twice.
* A late verified Twilio cost for a closed hold is settled once, through the existing settlement group.
* Nothing in this ticket deletes records or forgives amounts due.

## Who can do what

Only the system job closes holds or moves them to review. Admins see held items in the Twilio billing panel. Users can't change holds.

## Out of scope

* Stopping new holds for workspaces that aren't enrolled: ENG-14811.
* Automatic enrolment: ENG-14812.

## Done when

* A test with an expired accepted text hold and no possible wallet change shows the hold is closed as not collected, and a new text then sends.
* A test with an unknown wallet change shows the hold goes to needs review and still blocks, and it appears in the Twilio billing panel.
* A test where the Twilio cost arrives after the hold closed shows it's settled exactly once.
* A call hold with verified cost transfers its exposure, and an ambiguous call hold stays reserved.
* The send error for a billing block names the cause instead of "try again shortly".
* Each of the 121 rows from the manual repair is in closed or needs review, based on its own evidence, and none stays `settled` without a collection.

## Implementation context

* Safety check: unsettled-funding.ts
* Settlement skips expired locks and can debit directly: settle.ts lines 38 to 133 and 205 to 233
* Wallet changes and unknown outcomes: mutations.ts
* Hold states: phone-message-funding.ts
* Call exposure and its reconciliation: exposure.ts and call-discovery.ts
* Existing recovery for unsent holds only: recovery.ts
* Generic error: errors.ts and funding.ts
